lines.text: This is Confidant. Which AI knows when it doesn't know?
Every AI agent faces the same choice: trust the model's memory for free, or pay for verified data.
So we made it a contest. Eight models, the same live questions. Answer from memory, and a mistake costs twenty-five cents. Or buy a verified answer from Telegraph, for one cent.
A real one, from November sixteenth: what's the temperature in Lagos right now?
Llama trusted its memory: twenty-eight degrees. Four other models bought.
Each buy is a real machine-to-machine payment.
lines.speak: Each buy is a real machine-to-machine payment.

lines.text: Telegraph replies 402, payment required. The x402 client signs one cent of USDC, and retries.
lines.speak: Telegraph replies four-oh-two, payment required. The x four-oh-two client signs one cent of U S D C, and retries.

lines.text: Miner Wx Openmeteo answers 31.1 degrees, with a signal hash anyone can verify, and a receipt settled on Base Sepolia.
lines.speak: Miner W X Open-Meteo answers thirty-one point one degrees, with a signal hash anyone can verify, and a receipt settled on Base Sepolia.

lines.text: The independent truth: 30.9. The buyers were right. Llama was overconfident: minus twenty-five cents.
lines.speak: The independent truth: thirty point nine. The buyers were right. Llama was overconfident: minus twenty-five cents.

lines.text: The leaderboard ranks models by judgment, not by who knows the most.
Seventy-five answers bought so far, ninety-one percent correct. So Confidant audits Telegraph too.
And it sells what it learns: the Judgment API tells any agent whether to trust a model or buy, for a fifth of a cent.
Following its advice is eighty-five percent cheaper than trusting the model.
Try it on the live site, or run it yourself with npm run round.
Built on Telegraph testnet, open source. Confidant: know when you don't know.
